summary: Corrected a retained claim in the recovery-authority finding after checking it against the source. The prepare-recovery rejection path (handlePrepareReply, lines 1216-1219) contains no repair at all - it counts the nack and returns - whereas the makeBallot-plus-bcastPrepare restarts I had attributed to it live in the proposal-phase handlers (handlePreAcceptReply lines 855-868 and handleAcceptReply lines 1016-1033), each executed only while r.IsLeader is true, and makeBallot's climb above maxRecvBallot is gated on the same flag. The behavior entry was revised under its existing id with the semantic difference recorded (changed_premise) and the affected interpretation named (affected_uses), and the recovery-authority account now cites the correct sites and adds this as counterevidence: the conclusion that a blocked, non-designated recoverer stays inert is unchanged and in fact now rests on a simpler basis, since the path it uses has no repair rather than a gated one. With that, the run's accounts are internally consistent and evidence-linked: four explained questions (including the refuted wrong-row-write suspicion as a recorded negative result), three asserted defects each backed by executed receipts whose cited claims have been spot-checked against the fixed source, one holds account for the client-completion protection, and six knowledge entries carrying their receipts and boundary conditions. The remaining limits noted in those accounts are the single configuration and instance exercised, the harness's explicit delivery and direct entry-point calls, and the reachability condition that a peer of the instance must fail for the accept broadcast to reach a replica that never pre-accepted.
